supersedes_reason: v2 base execution exposed a finite-stream fixture flaw: baseline omitted trailing incomplete rows but the fixture did not supply enough later rows to force the split group member into a second emitted batch. v2 therefore did not distinguish streaming loss from cross-microbatch group splitting. v2 result is retained and not used as evidence for the split claim.
question: Do pinned production batchers split same-rollout members across emitted microbatches under a forced boundary, and can a candidate preserve all rows/groups within actual fixed-count and token-budget constraints?

fixed_count.purpose: A3+B2 forces a boundary after B0 in the per-row batcher; C2+D1 then forces a second batch so B1 is observed in a different emitted batch; E1 makes the candidate EOF tail co-packable with D.

token_budget.purpose: Greedy per-row LPT puts A=[7,3], B0=4 alongside A, then cannot fit B1=6 and emits B split. Following groups force a second emitted batch while remaining globally feasible; exact repacking can place A=[7,3], B=[4,6] and C=[2,2], D=[9,1] without splitting.

method.execution: AST-extract and execute only _balance_by_squared_length, FixedCountBatcher, and TokenBudgetBatcher from the source checkout under test; only class base/logger are stubbed.
method.comparison: Run unchanged script from pristine pinned base and local candidate checkout.

primary_invariants: all fixture rows emitted exactly once
every rollout ID appears in exactly one emitted microbatch
each emitted rank row is nonempty
fixed-count microbatch has at most 4 samples
token-budget row has at most 10 tokens
success_rule: Pinned base must demonstrate a group spanning two emitted microbatches in both fixtures; the group-aware candidate must satisfy all invariants in both fixtures.
rejection_rule: Candidate loses or duplicates any row, splits a rollout, emits an empty rank, or violates a declared capacity.
claim_limits: Only two finite fixtures against actual extracted production definitions are tested.
No full TRL import, Trainer/optimizer step, distributed collective, epoch stopping, throughput, prevalence, task-success or model-capability claim.
A pass does not alone make an upstream patch ready.
